title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DELLA'S TRUCK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Della Harmon, an X-ray tech from Muskogee, Oklahoma.
Della can see right through a person. But she can't see a thing under the hood of a truck.
And her late dad's old pickup had been sitting in the barn for fifteen years.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: OLD BLUE
segments.quote: Do not wait; the time will never be just right.
segments.author: Napoleon Hill
lines: Dad called it Old Blue. Four flat tires. A family of raccoons in the seat.
Della wanted to drive Mom to the lake in it, for her seventy-fifth birthday in May.
She kept saying, someday. Then she found Dad's old copy of Napoleon Hill in the glove box, one line circled:
Do not wait; the time will never be just right.
That night, she evicted the raccoons. Politely.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: DUMB QUESTIONS
segments.quote: The scientist is not a person who gives the right answers, he's one who asks the right questions.
segments.author: Claude Lévi-Strauss
lines: She bought a repair manual and read it like a mystery novel. She understood the cover.
At work, the radiologist had a line by Claude Lévi-Strauss, a French scientist, pinned on his wall:
The scientist is not a person who gives the right answers, he's one who asks the right questions.
So Della stopped pretending. She asked Ernie at the parts store a hundred dumb questions. He answered every one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE STUCK BOLT
segments.quote: Give me a place to stand, and I shall move the world.
segments.author: Archimedes
lines: One rusty bolt would not move. Della pulled until her face turned the color of the truck.
Ernie slid a long pipe over her wrench and quoted Archimedes, the old Greek genius:
Give me a place to stand, and I shall move the world.
She stood on the bumper, leaned on the pipe, and the bolt turned like butter.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE SMOKE
segments.quote: Every failure is a step to success.
segments.author: William Whewell
lines: In March, she turned the key. Old Blue coughed, shook, and blew black smoke over the whole yard.
The neighbor's dog left town.
Della almost sold it right there. Then Ernie quoted William Whewell, an English scientist:
Every failure is a step to success.
She wrote down every step she took, and started again. Slower. Smarter.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BROTHER
segments.author: Aesop
lines: Her brother Gene in Tulsa hadn't really talked to her since Dad's funeral.
One Saturday, he showed up with Dad's red toolbox and said, You're doing it wrong.
Mom just smiled and quoted Aesop's old story about the bundle of sticks:
Union gives strength.
So they worked side by side every weekend. They argued about wrenches, and laughed about Dad.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE LAKE
segments.quote: The longer I live the more beautiful life becomes.
segments.author: Frank Lloyd Wright
lines: On Mom's birthday, Old Blue started on the first try.
Halfway to the lake, it got a flat. All three of them stood by the road, laughing.
They ate the cake right there on the tailgate. Mom looked at the water and quoted Frank Lloyd Wright:
The longer I live the more beautiful life becomes.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start now. Ask. Lean in. Try again. Work together. Enjoy it.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start now. Ask questions. Lean in. Try again, smarter. Work together. And enjoy the ride.
I tried to change my own oil once. My driveway still remembers.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
